title_en: Li Zhongping v. Nanjing University of the Arts and Jiangsu Zhenze Law Firm — dispute over infringement of the right to reputation
ruling_gist_en: A law firm or a lawyer that accepts a client's entrustment to issue a lawyer's statement shall conduct necessary review and verification of the truthfulness and legality of the content of the statement requested to be published by the client. If the law firm or lawyer fails to fulfill the necessary review obligation and issues a signed lawyer's statement as requested by the client, and if such lawyer's statement is contrary to fact and infringes upon another person's right to reputation, the law firm or the lawyer shall bear joint and several tort liability for such infringement.
keywords_en: Civil; Dispute over right to reputation; First instance; Basic People's Court; Jiangsu Province; Natural person; Legal person; General Principles of the Civil Law; Whether a lawyer's statement constitutes infringement of the right to reputation; Whether a law firm bears joint and several liability; Support for plaintiff; Lawyer's statement; Infringement of right to reputation; Entrustment relationship; Duty of review; Tort liability; Right to reputation; Dispute over a law firm's infringement of the right to reputation
full_text_en:
Li Zhongping v. Nanjing University of the Arts and Jiangsu Zhenze Law Firm — dispute over infringement of the right to reputation

Ruling Summary

Where a law firm or lawyer publishes a lawyer's statement upon the entrustment of a client, it/he shall carry out the necessary review and verification of whether the content of the statement requested to be published by the client is true and lawful. If the law firm or lawyer publishes a signed lawyer's statement in accordance with the client's request without performing the necessary review obligations, and such lawyer's statement deviates from the facts and infringes upon another person's right to reputation, the law firm or lawyer shall bear joint and several tort liability therefor.

Plaintiff: Li Zhongping, male, 46 years old, Han ethnicity, unemployed, residing at Tianjin New Village, Nanjing.

Defendant: Nanjing University of the Arts, domiciled at Huju North Road, Nanjing.
Legal Representative: Feng Jianqin, President of the University.

Defendant: Jiangsu Zhenze Law Firm, domiciled at Zhongshan South Road, Nanjing.
Person in Charge: Li Xiaobing, Director of the Law Firm.

Plaintiff Li Zhongping, because he had a dispute with Defendant Nanjing University of the Arts (hereinafter referred to as "the University of the Arts") and Defendant Jiangsu Zhenze Law Firm (hereinafter referred to as "Zhenze Law Firm") over infringement of the right to reputation, instituted an action in the Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.

Plaintiff Li Zhongping alleged: On December 1, 2003, the Plaintiff entered into a two-year agreement with the Defendant University of the Arts. The agreement stipulated that the Plaintiff would raise his own funds, premises, and equipment, operate independently with separate accounting, and manage the training center of the University of the Arts autonomously, and the University of the Arts appointed the Plaintiff as Deputy Director of the training center. On May 1, 2004, the Defendant University of the Arts renewed the agreement with the Plaintiff, still appointing the Plaintiff as Deputy Director of the Art Center, with the Plaintiff to pay an annual intangible asset usage fee of RMB 15,000 to the University of the Arts. During this period, the Plaintiff, in his capacity as Deputy Director of the training center of the University of the Arts, entered into contracts and conducted art training activities, all of which were recognized by the University of the Arts. On July 15, 2006, lawyers Li Xiaobing and Zhao Zhiying of the Defendant Zhenze Law Firm, purporting to act on the entrustment of the University of the Arts, published a statement in *Yangtze Evening News*, publicly claiming that the Plaintiff was neither a staff member of the University of the Arts nor a staff member of its training center, that the University of the Arts had never authorized the Plaintiff personally to conduct activities on behalf of its training center, and that it would not recognize any activities conducted by the Plaintiff personally in the name of the training center of the University of the Arts. The purpose of this act by the two Defendants was to make the public believe that the Plaintiff was a swindler and to discredit the Plaintiff. After the publication of the statement, relatives and friends of the Plaintiff called to inquire, believing that the Plaintiff had been engaging in illegal activities and swindling in the name of the University of the Arts. The Plaintiff felt extremely distressed and pained. Zhenze Law Firm, knowing full well that the Plaintiff was a staff member of the University of the Arts, nevertheless issued the statement jointly with the University of the Arts and should bear joint and several liability. In conclusion, the Plaintiff believes that the two Defendants intentionally concealed the truth, published a statement in the media, deceived the public, disparaged the Plaintiff's image, infringed upon his right to reputation, and caused him great mental suffering. Therefore, the Plaintiff requested the court to: 1. Order the two Defendants to remove the statement from the website of the training center of the University of the Arts and to publish an apology in the same section of *Yangtze Evening News* and on the training center website; 2. Order the two Defendants to pay the Plaintiff RMB 20,000 as compensation for mental distress and to bear the litigation costs of this case.

Defendants University of the Arts and Zhenze Law Firm uniformly defended: In the lawyer's statement involved in this case published by the two Defendants, there was neither any evaluation insulting the personality of the Plaintiff Li Zhongping nor any false information fabricated concerning the Plaintiff's morals; there was neither insult nor defamation of the Plaintiff, nor any disclosure of the Plaintiff's privacy. At the time of the publication of the lawyer's statement, the Plaintiff was indeed no longer a staff member of the University of the Arts, and the University of the Arts had never authorized Li Zhongping personally to conduct activities on behalf of its training center. Therefore, it cannot be determined that the two Defendants infringed upon the Plaintiff's right to reputation. The Defendants requested the court to dismiss the Plaintiff's claims.

The Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing found the following facts at first instance:

On December 1, 2003, the Industry Development Department, a subordinate unit of the Defendant University of the Arts, entered into an agreement with the Plaintiff Li Zhongping, employing Li Zhongping as Deputy Director of the training center subordinate to the University of the Arts, in charge of art training. On May 1 of the following year, the parties renewed the agreement, continuing to employ Li Zhongping as Deputy Director of the training center and stipulating that Li Zhongping would pay an annual intangible asset usage fee of RMB 15,000 to the University of the Arts. On October 28, 2005, the University of the Arts unilaterally decided to terminate the aforementioned agreement with Li Zhongping. Thereafter, Li Zhongping continued to engage in art training work at the training center of the University of the Arts. On July 7, 2006, a conflict arose between the parties, and the training center of the University of the Arts issued a written notice to Li Zhongping, requiring him to complete the handover procedures. On the 15th of that month, the University of the Arts entrusted the Defendant Zhenze Law Firm to publish the lawyer's statement involved in the case. The lawyers of that firm, relying solely on the unilateral statements of the University of the Arts and without making necessary inquiries or verification with the Plaintiff, published a public statement in *Yangtze Evening News* entitled "Lawyer's Statement Authorized by the Training Center of Nanjing University of the Arts," the content of which read as follows: "Lawyers Li Xiaobing and Zhao Zhiying, the permanent legal advisors of Nanjing University of the Arts, upon the entrustment of the Art Training Center of Nanjing University of the Arts, hereby publish the following lawyer's statement: The Art Training Center of Nanjing University of the Arts is a higher education training institution established upon application by Nanjing University of the Arts and recorded with the Education Department of Jiangsu Province. All fees charged by the Training Center for enrollment are accompanied by Jiangsu Provincial Administrative Institutional Fee Receipts stamped with the financial seal of the University of the Arts, and all contracts entered into by the Training Center are sealed with its official chop. Li Zhongping is neither a staff member of the University of the Arts nor a staff member of its Training Center. The Training Center has never authorized Li Zhongping personally to conduct activities on behalf of the Training Center, and it will not recognize any activities conducted by Li Zhongping personally in the name of the Training Center. So stated hereby! Lawyers Li Xiaobing and Zhao Zhiying of Jiangsu Zhenze Law Firm." Thereafter, the statement was also reproduced on the website of the training center of the University of the Arts and had not been removed as of the date of the court hearing.

It was also found that the Industry Development Department and the Training Center are both subordinate units of the University of the Arts and do not have independent legal personality.

The above facts are confirmed by the agreements, appointment letters, text of the lawyer's statement, downloaded copies of relevant web pages, and other evidence submitted by the parties and lawfully cross-examined, as well as the statements of the parties, which are sufficient for determination.

The issues in dispute in this case are: 1. Whether the lawyer's statement published by the Defendants University of the Arts and Zhenze Law Firm constituted an infringement upon the Plaintiff Li Zhongping's right to reputation; 2. If it constituted an infringement upon the right to reputation, whether Zhenze Law Firm should bear joint and several tort liability therefor.

The Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing held at first instance:

I. The lawyer's statement published by the Defendants University of the Arts and Zhenze Law Firm constituted an infringement upon the Plaintiff Li Zhongping's right to reputation.

Reputation, or name or renown, refers to the comprehensive evaluation of a natural person or legal person by society. The right to reputation is the right of a citizen or legal person to participate in social life and competition in reliance on his/her/its own reputation, and belongs to the spiritual personality rights of citizens or legal persons. Its content is that citizens or legal persons enjoy (control) their own reputation without being hindered by others. A good reputation is an important condition for citizens or legal persons to participate in social life and competition. Infringement upon reputation necessarily directly impedes and affects the qualification of citizens or legal persons to participate in social competition. Therefore, the law protects the right to reputation of citizens or legal persons from infringement by others. Article 101 of the *General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China* provides: "Citizens and legal persons enjoy the right to reputation. The personality dignity of citizens shall be protected by law. It is prohibited to damage the reputation of citizens or legal persons by means such as insult or defamation." Article 140 of the *Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation)* provides: "Publicizing another person's privacy in written or oral form, or fabricating facts to openly vilify another person's personality, or damaging another person's reputation by means such as insult or defamation, thereby causing a certain impact, shall be deemed an act infringing upon the citizen's right to reputation. Slandering or defaming the reputation of a legal person in written or oral form, thereby causing damage to the legal person, shall be deemed an act infringing upon the legal person's right to reputation."

According to the facts of this case, the content of the lawyer's statement published by the Defendants University of the Arts and Zhenze Law Firm was inconsistent with the facts, causing a reduction in the social evaluation of the Plaintiff Li Zhongping, and constituted fabricating facts to openly vilify another person's personality and damage another person's reputation, causing a certain impact, thus constituting an infringement upon Li Zhongping's right to reputation.

First, through the agreement entered into with the Industry Development Department subordinate to the Defendant University of the Arts, the Plaintiff Li Zhongping was employed by the University of the Arts as Deputy Director of the training center subordinate to the University of the Arts, in charge of art training. From December 1, 2003 to October 28, 2005, the Plaintiff served as Deputy Director of the training center. Thereafter, although the University of the Arts unilaterally decided on October 28, 2005 to terminate the aforementioned agreement with the Plaintiff, the Plaintiff continued to engage in art training work at the training center for a period of nine months until July 7, 2006. Therefore, it can be determined that the content of the lawyer's statement jointly published by the University of the Arts and the Defendant Zhenze Law Firm — that "Li Zhongping is neither a staff member of the University of the Arts nor a staff member of its Training Center" — was inconsistent with the facts. According to the *Agreement* entered into on December 1, 2003 between the Industry Development Department of the Defendant University of the Arts and the Plaintiff Li Zhongping, the Industry Development Department employed Li Zhongping as Deputy Director of the training center subordinate to the University of the Arts, in charge of art training. Li Zhongping was to raise his own funds, premises, and equipment, operate autonomously, assume sole responsibility for profits and losses, maintain independent financial accounting, and bear all external debts himself, which were unrelated to the training center. It is evident that the agreement was essentially a piggybacking agreement, and the purpose of Li Zhongping in entering into the agreement with the Industry Development Department of the University of the Arts was to conduct training activities externally in the name of the training center of the University of the Arts. Therefore, the execution of the agreement should be deemed as the Industry Development Department of the University of the Arts consenting to Li Zhongping's use of the name of the training center of the University of the Arts in conducting external business. The agreement also stipulated that the Industry Development Department of the University of the Arts would provide Li Zhongping with uniform fee receipts supervised by the Provincial Department of Finance, with the external name to be used as "Art Training Center, University of the Arts." This also indicates that the Industry Development Department of the University of the Arts consented to Li Zhongping's use of the name of the training center of the University of the Arts in conducting external training business activities. The parties renewed the *Agreement* on May 1, 2004, which stipulated: "Li Zhongping shall pay an annual intangible asset usage fee of RMB 15,000 to the University of the Arts, and Li Zhongping shall have the right to independently employ personnel, sign labor contracts, and handle pension insurance." This further proves that the Industry Development Department of the University of the Arts authorized Li Zhongping to conduct external training business activities in the name of the training center of the University of the Arts. Given that the Industry Development Department and the Training Center are both subordinate units of the University of the Arts, neither having independent legal personality, and the University of the Arts has no objection to the legality and validity of the two aforementioned agreements, the two agreements entered into between the Industry Development Department of the University of the Arts and Li Zhongping are directly binding on the University of the Arts. The authorization by the Industry Development Department of the University of the Arts that "Li Zhongping may conduct external training business activities in the name of the University of the Arts" may be deemed as authorization by the University of the Arts to Li Zhongping. In summary, it can be determined that the content of the lawyer's statement involved in the case — that "the Training Center has never authorized Li Zhongping personally to conduct activities on behalf of the Training Center, and it will not recognize any activities conducted by Li Zhongping personally in the name of the Training Center" — was inconsistent with the facts.

Second, the public publication of the aforementioned content inconsistent with the facts in the lawyer's statement caused the relatives and friends of the Plaintiff Li Zhongping, as well as the units and individuals who had business dealings with Li Zhongping, and all other persons who read the statement, to mistakenly believe that Li Zhongping had been impersonating a staff member of the Defendant University of the Arts to swindle and conduct illegal training business activities, leading to Li Zhongping being subjected to contempt and criticism, thereby reducing his social evaluation and causing damage to his reputation. Although the Plaintiff did not adduce evidence to prove the actual damage consequences caused by the aforementioned act of infringement upon the right to reputation, it can be determined based on common knowledge of social life that the objective fact of the publication of the lawyer's statement in public media and on the internet was sufficient to cause the consequence of damage to Li Zhongping's reputation.

In conclusion, the act of the training center subordinate to the Defendant University of the Arts entrusting the Defendant Zhenze Law Firm to publish the lawyer's statement involved in the case infringed upon the Plaintiff Li Zhongping's right to reputation. Since the training center subordinate to the University of the Arts is only a department of the University of the Arts, does not have independent legal personality, and cannot assume civil liability externally in its own name, its tort liability shall be borne by the University of the Arts in accordance with the law.

II. The Defendant Zhenze Law Firm, by accepting the entrustment of the Defendant University of the Arts to publish the lawyer's statement involved in the case, constituted a joint tort and shall bear joint and several tort liability.

A lawyer's statement is a written document published by a law firm or lawyer, in the name of the law firm or lawyer, through the media or other forms, to publicly disclose relevant facts to society or evaluate relevant legal issues, based on the authorization of the client and for a certain purpose to achieve a certain effect. Because a lawyer's statement is published externally in the name of the law firm or lawyer, its content is inevitably perceived by the public as professional opinions expressed by lawyers as legal experts. Therefore, lawyer's statements often enjoy high credibility and have a relatively greater impact on the public. Relying on their trust in the legal profession, the public is also more likely to accept and believe the content of lawyer's statements. Therefore, when a law firm or lawyer accepts a client's entrustment to publicly publish a lawyer's statement, it/he shall perform the necessary obligation to review the facts involved in the statement. If the law firm or lawyer publishes a signed lawyer's statement in accordance with the client's request without performing the necessary review obligations, and such lawyer's statement deviates from the facts and infringes upon another person's right to reputation, the law firm or lawyer constitutes a joint tort and shall bear joint and several tort liability.

According to the facts of this case, the Defendant Zhenze Law Firm and its lawyers, relying solely on the unilateral statements of the Defendant University of the Arts, without making necessary review, without conducting necessary investigation and verification with the Plaintiff Li Zhongping, published the lawyer's statement involving the case that contained false content, thus having fault, constituting a joint tort, and shall bear joint and several tort liability. The acts of the lawyers Li Xiaobing and Zhao Zhiying, who signed the lawyer's statement involved in the case, were acts performed in the course of their duties on behalf of Zhenze Law Firm; therefore, the legal liability therefor shall be borne by Zhenze Law Firm in accordance with the law.

In summary, the content of the lawyer's statement involved in the case was false and infringed upon the Plaintiff Li Zhongping's right to reputation. The Defendants University of the Arts and Zhenze Law Firm shall bear joint and several tort liability. Given that the two Defendants did not directly use words accusing Li Zhongping in the lawyer's statement involved in the case, the court discretionarily determines that the two Defendants shall pay Li Zhongping RMB 3,000 as compensation for mental distress. Accordingly, the Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing, in accordance with Article 101, paragraph 2 of Article 106, paragraph 1 of Article 120, Article 130, items (9) and (10) of paragraph 2 of Article 134 of the *General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China*, Article 23 of the *Law of the People's Republic of China on Lawyers*, Article 7 and Article 10 of the *Answers of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Adjudication of Cases Involving Disputes over the Right to Reputation*, and Article 10 of the *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Determination of Compensation Liability for Mental Damage in Civil Torts*, rendered judgment on October 26, 2006:

1. The Defendants University of the Arts and Zhenze Law Firm shall immediately cease the infringement and, within the time limit after the judgment takes effect, immediately delete the "Lawyer's Statement Authorized by the Art Training Center of Nanjing University of the Arts" published on the website of the training center subordinate to the Defendant University of the Arts;

2. The Defendants University of the Arts and Zhenze Law Firm shall, within fifteen days after the judgment takes effect, publish an apology in *Yangtze Evening News* and on the website of the training center subordinate to the Defendant University of the Arts (the content thereof shall be submitted to the court for review in advance);

3. The Defendants University of the Arts and Zhenze Law Firm shall pay the Plaintiff Li Zhongping RMB 3,000 as compensation for mental distress within fifteen days after the judgment takes effect.

Both the University of the Arts and Zhenze Law Firm were dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance and appealed to the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court. Their main grounds of appeal were: 1. At the time of the publication of the lawyer's statement involved in the case, the Respondent Li Zhongping was indeed no longer a staff member of the University of the Arts, and the University of the Arts had indeed never authorized Li Zhongping personally to conduct training activities on behalf of the training center subordinate to the University of the Arts. Therefore, the basic content of the lawyer's statement involved in the case was true; 2. The lawyer's statement involved in the case jointly published by the University of the Arts and Zhenze Law Firm merely disclosed general information externally, did not involve any evaluation of the Respondent's morals, and even less contained any content insulting or defaming the Respondent's personality, and therefore did not constitute infringement upon reputation; 3. The Respondent did not adduce evidence to prove that the lawyer's statement involved in the case caused any damage to his reputation. In conclusion, they requested the appellate court to set aside the judgment of first instance and to amend the judgment to dismiss the Respondent's claims according to law.

The Respondent Li Zhongping argued: 1. The Appellant University of the Arts twice entered into agreements with the Respondent in 2003 and 2004, employing the Respondent as Deputy Director of its subordinate training center, in charge of art training work, and expressly authorized the Respondent to conduct external training business on behalf of the training center of the University of the Arts. Therefore, the basic content of the lawyer's statement involved in the case was contrary to the facts; 2. After seeing the lawyer's statement involved in the case, the Respondent's relatives, friends, and business partners mistakenly believed that the Respondent had been impersonating the name of the training center of the University of the Arts for years to swindle and engage in illegal training activities to defraud money, and they repeatedly called to interrogate the Respondent. The Respondent felt extremely wronged and suffered great mental pain and torment. The Respondent's reputation suffered actual damage due to the false report in the lawyer's statement involved in the case. The trial court correctly found the facts, correctly applied the law, and its judgment was not improper. The Respondent requested the appellate court to dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, upon second instance, confirmed the facts found at first instance.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court held at second instance:

Reputation refers to society's comprehensive evaluation of a natural person or legal entity. The right to reputation is the right of a citizen or legal entity to participate in social life and social competition based on their reputation. A good reputation is an important condition for citizens or legal entities to participate in social life and social competition, and infringement of reputation inevitably directly hinders and affects the qualifications of citizens or legal entities to participate in social competition. Therefore, the law protects the right to reputation of citizens and legal entities from infringement by others. In this case, the Appellants, the Art Institute and Zhenze Law Firm, jointly published the lawyer's statement at issue. Without clearly specifying the start and end dates, the statement vaguely and generally asserted that the Respondent, Li Zhongping, was "neither a member of the Art Institute nor a member of the Nanyi Training Center" and that "the Training Center of the Art Institute has never authorized Li Zhongping to conduct any external activities in the name of the Nanyi Training Center." The content of this statement was inconsistent with the facts. The Art Institute and Zhenze Law Firm should have foreseen that their actions might result in damage to Li Zhongping's reputation, but they nevertheless published the said lawyer's statement in newspapers and on websites, thereby lowering Li Zhongping's social evaluation. The above-mentioned actions of the Art Institute and Zhenze Law Firm lack any justifiable defense or grounds for excluding wrongfulness and have constituted an infringement of Li Zhongping's right to reputation. The court of first instance, taking into account the degree of fault of the Art Institute and Zhenze Law Firm, the circumstances, consequences, and impact of the infringing acts, ordered the two Appellants to cease the infringement, make an apology, and compensate the Respondent with RMB 3,000 for moral damages. This decision was not improper. The judgment of the first instance found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly, and should be upheld according to law. The grounds of appeal of the two Appellants are untenable and should be rejected according to law.

Accordingly, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on April 3, 2007:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

This judgment is final.
